To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have measured the effective temperature of the brightest known roAp star, β CrB A, to be 7980 K, with a 2.3% uncertainty.
the interferometrically determined limb-darkened diameter of the primary component of β CrB is 0.699 mas, and that the effective temperature of this component is 7980 K.
we have determined the radius of the primary component in the binary roAp star β CrB to be 2.63 R�, with a precision of 3.4%.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the determination of the effective temperatures of Ap stars.
the determination of the fundamental stellar parameters of the roAp star α Circini (α Cir).
the development of the interferometric technique for measuring the angular diameters of stars, and the application of this technique to stars of interest for asteroseismic studies.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the effective temperature of the roAp star β CrB is 7980 ±180 K.
the effective temperature of the roAp star β CrB has been determined to be 7980 ±180 K, and the uncertainty is now 2.3%.
we now have a reliable and accurate determination of the effective surface gravity of a roAp star, but that the effective temperature is still somewhat uncertain.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the interferometric observations are very important for determining the radius of the roAp star β CrB A and the VLT/NACOs observations are important for separating the flux contribution of the two components.

our new interferometric data for β CrB, in combination with new VLT/NACOS observations of α Cir, have enabled nearly model-independent determination for the effective temperatures of two of the three brightest roAp stars.
the effective temperature of Ap stars is now known to an accuracy of 2% or better for the brightest stars.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the interferometric technique is a very powerful tool to constrain the effective temperature of Ap stars.
interferometric observations of Ap stars with a range of effective temperatures are needed in order to improve the accuracy of Teff calibrations.
interferometric measurements can yield precise and accurate stellar radii for bright stars.
